relevance_note: The paper describes the SSADHD natural history study and reports identifiable patients with ALDH5A1 variants, e.g. "The genotype was compound heterozygous c.1294A>C (p.Met432Leu); c.610-2A>G."
method_note: Study-level cohort paper on succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency with no per-patient table: Table 1 is the Clinical Severity Score key (no patients) and Table 2 gives only group counts (N = 16 pediatric and N = 9 adolescent/adult BCH subjects, with percentages), so no rows were created from Table 2. No table was transcribed by script; every value was copied by hand from the Markdown. Labels follow the fixed order: no patient has a label of the paper's own, so the three people first described in the Results without any label take rule 6 ('unnamed person <k>' in order of first mention) and the previously published boy takes rule 4. Mapping of the made-up labels: 'unnamed person 1' = 'A single patient had the maximum severity level (5 of 25)' (most severe patient, first mention, Results); 'unnamed person 2' = 'A single patient had a normal IQ measurement and also had the least severity on the global scale (20 of 25)'; 'unnamed person 3' = the patient of Figure 5, '**Figure 5**: EEG in an 8 year old patient with SSADHD.' (first mention is in the Tables and figures section); 'ref (Yamakawa et al 2012) patient' = the '23-month old boy' of the Discussion, in scope as a previously published person because the paper gives sex, age and features for him. Group-level statements and counts name no individual and were used neither for rows nor to exclude anything: 28 recruited subjects, the 143-patient registry, 55-patient enrollment target, 25 EEG subjects with diffuse background slowing in 16 (mild in all cases), focal spikes in two subjects (ages 5 and 9, without history of seizures), sharp waves in two, 21 with neuropsychological evaluations, 20 with autism scales, 28 with severity scores, the two BCH cohort columns of Table 2, and 'in all subjects' for the neuroimaging and MR spectroscopy findings. The abstract statements ('Epilepsy is present in half', 'half scored as having ASD', 'MR spectroscopy showed elevations in the GABA/NAA ratio in all regions studied') are cohort-level and were attributed to nobody. Variant fields come only from each person's own sentence; the paper reports no parental testing for any variant, so every inheritance value is 'not reported'. Uncertainties: (1) the three 'single patient'/figure patients may be members of the cohorts described only in counts, but they are the only people described individually, so they are the rows; (2) the most severe patient's two variants stand in one sentence ('The genotype was compound heterozygous c.1294A>C (p.Met432Leu); c.610-2A>G.'), so zygosity 'compound heterozygous' was taken from that sentence for both rows, while no variant class was recorded for c.610-2A>G because the paper calls only c.1294A>C a missense variant; (3) no sex, age at last evaluation or treatment is given for 'unnamed person 1' and 'unnamed person 2', and no age, sex or variant is given for 'unnamed person 3'; (4) the Discussion sentence about the 23-month old boy could be read as attributing c.1294A>C to him, but the attribution is indirect ('the missense variant c.1294A>C (p.Met432Leu) in the most severely affected patient was also published in a 23-month old boy'), so his variant row keeps 'not reported' as printed for him; (5) the acronym 'SADH Association' in the Methods appears to be a typo for SSADH Association, left as printed and unused.
